newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreign car companies fight back in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Foreign car companies fight back in South Korea.

text.p: Foreign carmakers, whose sales in South Korea have been hit by a "frugality campaign", said on Wednesday they were fighting back by opening more showrooms, cutting prices and introducing new models.
"Our biggest concern is that foreign cars have been targeted in the frugality campaign," said Wayne Chumley, president of Chrysler Korea Sales Limited.
"But we aim to sell 4,000 units this year, up from about 2,200 units last year," he said in an interview ahead of the formal opening on Thursday of the '97 Seoul Motor Show.
Chumley said Chrysler would increase its sales outlets in South Korea to 28 by the end of this year from 23 and to 50 by 2000.
Chrysler now sells Neon and Stratus sedans, a range of sports utility vehicles, such as the Jeep Wrangler, and plans to add the Viper coupe to its sales list.
The European Union and the United States have attacked South Korea's government over what they call its complicity in the "frugality campaign" targeting foreign consumer goods, including cars.
The campaign, spearheaded by civic and religious groups, is designed to curb imports and reduce a bloated trade deficit.
"The frugality campaign is creating a consumer bias that imported cars are luxury goods," said Gerhard Pils, chairman of the automotive committee at the European Union Chamber of Commerce in Korea.
"Wider market opening will make us all winners," he said.

U.S. trade officials have charged that South Koreans who buy foreign vehicles are subject to surprise tax audits and other harrassments. Foreign car sales account for just more than one percent of the total in South Korea.
James Tessada, president of Ford Motor Korea, said Ford plans to sell 3,500 cars this year against 986 in 1996.
"We cut prices for Taurus sedans by about 15 percent. We are introducing new models for this year, including '97 Mercury Mystique and Continental sedans," Tessada said.
Ford now offers Taurus and Mondeo sedans, Mustang convertibles and Explorer sport utility vehicles.
"Our price cuts are affordable and reasonable for us and consumers," he said.
Domestic newspapers reported on Wednesday that South Korean carmakers were considering anti-dumping complaints against their foreign rivals because of the price cuts.
Ford Korea plans to raise the number of its showrooms, which sell cars and provide after-sales services as a one-stop system, to 21 by the end of this year from eight.
The EU Chamber of Commerce's Pils said an economic slowdown and social pressure against foreign autos were hurting BMW sales, even though sales this year would exceed last year's total of 1,447.
He said BMW planned to add three to four more showrooms this year on top of its existing 17.
BMW recently began marketing its two-seater roadster Z3 cars and plans to offer its top-of-the-line L7 luxury sedans.
South Korea imported 25,148 cars last year, which accounted for 1.5 percent of total domestic sales of 1.64 million units, according to figures by the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association.
South Korea exported 1.21 million vehicles in 1996, the association said.
